key_insight: StableWorld pinpoints why current interactive video models suffer spatial drift and scene collapse over long interactions and introduces stability-focused design choices that keep generated worlds temporally consistent and controllable.
problem_solved: Mitigates instability and temporal degradation (spatial drift, scene collapse) in long‑horizon interactive video generation driven by camera movements and text prompts, enabling persistent, coherent video worlds across extended interactions.
method: Analyze failure modes in long interactive sequences to quantify temporal degradation and identify sources of instability.

Incorporate stability-focused components (e.g., temporal-consistency objectives, memory/latent alignment, and explicit conditioning on camera/interaction signals) to preserve geometry and identity over time.
Train and evaluate on long-horizon interactive scenarios to enforce smooth transitions and prevent cumulative drift during prolonged camera or prompt-driven behaviors.
impact: Enables practitioners to build more reliable, controllable interactive video systems (virtual production, simulation, embodied AI) that maintain scene integrity over long interactions, reducing artifacts and improving user trust.
visual_elements: Before/after sequence: short video-frame strip showing scene collapse in baseline vs stable output from StableWorld.
System diagram: blocks for input conditioning (camera + prompts), temporal consistency module (memory/latent alignment), and renderer/output pipeline.
Metric timeline: line chart comparing temporal-consistency metrics (e.g., identity/geometry drift) across long horizons for baseline vs StableWorld.
Icon set: camera, text prompt, clock (long-horizon), and shield (stability) to summarize core concepts.
paper_title: StableWorld: Towards Stable and Consistent Long Interactive Video Generation
paper_authors: Ying Yang, Zhengyao Lv, Tianlin Pan, Haofan Wang, Binxin Yang
